lines.meet: I'm Delroy, and I brew. Drink this, and don't ask what's in it, yuh wouldn't thank me.
lines.meet_neighbour: Wah gwaan, neighbour. Yuh live on the Bay too, I see yuh on the gallery. Delroy, the old baker.
lines.ask_home: Tell me, where yuh from? I like to know where a person learned to eat.
lines.ask_work: Yuh have the look of a night worker. Tell me what yuh did, back home.
lines.answer_home: Kingston, near Spanish Town Road. My mother sold in the market and my father worked the docks.
lines.answer_work: Night baker, thirty-one years. In at eleven and out at seven, and I fed half of Kingston its breakfast.
lines.chat_food: Hard dough bread, still warm, with butter and a likkle cheese. Thirty-one years I made it, and I never once got tired of eating it.
lines.chat_sleep: I've never been awake at the same time as everybody else in my whole life. I sleep in the day like a cat, and I'm not sorry.
lines.chat_missing: Reggae on the radio at four in the morning, with the first loaves coming out. That was the best hour of every day.
lines.chat_here: A brew is a dough with different patience, that's all. This world just wanted somebody who knows how to wait for something to rise.
lines.tease_quiet: {name}, yuh so quiet I keep checking if yuh proving. Like dough, yuh understand, quiet and slow.
lines.tease_talker: {name}, yuh talk like a bakery at five in the morning, everybody at once. I like it, but my ears are old.
lines.tease_careful: {name}, yuh measure everything twice. Yuh would make a good baker, if yuh could stay awake.
lines.tease_bold: {name}, yuh rush like a man who's never had a loaf collapse on him. One day it will, and I'll laugh.
lines.tease_any: {name}, yuh drink every brew I give yuh and still pull a face. One day I'll make one that tastes nice, just to confuse yuh.
lines.tease_back: Ha, yuh got me, {name}. I'll let that one rise and come back to it.
lines.take_it_kindly: True, {name}, true. Marcia used to say the same, and she was always right.
lines.bristle: Leave that one alone, {name}. Some things nah fi joke about.
lines.apologise: Forgive an old man's mouth, it runs ahead of him. I'm sorry for it.
lines.double_down: Every word, and I'm too old to take things back now.
lines.needle_quiet: Yuh never tell me what's wrong, so I can't give yuh the right brew. Talk to me.
lines.needle_talker: Yuh talk so much, the brew boil over while I'm listening. Hush a likkle, nuh?
lines.needle_careful: Yuh poke and prod and the bread goes cold. Some things yuh just have to take out the oven.
lines.needle_bold: Yuh rush everything. A dough yuh rush comes out like a brick, and so do people.
lines.needle_any: Yuh won't drink what yuh given, and then yuh wonder why yuh feel bad. I'm tired of it.
lines.bite_back: I've been feeding people since before yuh was born. Don't tell me how to look after anybody.
lines.hurt: Mm, that one sit heavy, I won't lie. Give me a likkle while with it.
lines.laugh_off: Ha, the regulars said worse to me every morning for thirty years, and still came back for bread.
lines.confide: {name}, after my wife passed, I kept working nights, because the nights were when I missed her least. I've never said that to anybody here.
lines.listen: Sit, {name}, I'll pour yuh something. Talk as long as yuh need, I'm a night person.
lines.look_out: {name}, stay near me in there, so I can reach yuh with the brew. Nobody waits long on my watch.
lines.accept: Okay, {name}, your way. Don't tell anybody I listened.
lines.deflect: Mi soon come, {name}, I'm fine. A likkle knock never hurt an old baker.
lines.check_in: {name}, come, drink this. Tell me where it hurts, and don't lie to me.
lines.blame: Somebody rushed that, and it came out like a brick. I won't say who, but it wasn't me.
lines.thank: Yuh pulled me back from the edge there. Thank yuh, I'll bake yuh something special.
lines.brush_off: It's nothing at all. Drink up, and don't make a face.
lines.worry: {name}, yuh frighten me there. Sit down and drink this, all of it.
lines.handed_down: This one was yours, I think. I'll keep it safe, like a good starter.
lines.hand_fine: Keep it, keep it, it suits yuh. An old baker needs an apron and a spoon, that's all.
lines.hand_sulk: Nobody ask me about that. I'll let it go, but I noticed.
lines.turn_friendly: {name}, yuh good company on a long night. There'll always be a cup for yuh at my pitch.
lines.turn_friends: {name}, yuh family now. When I bake again, yuh get the first loaf out the oven.
lines.turn_grating: We don't rise the same, yuh and me. That's all right, we'll work around it.
lines.turn_rivals: I'll keep yuh alive because that's my job. Don't expect a story by the fire.
lines.make_up: Come, {name}, sit with me. Whatever was between us, let it cool on the rack, and we start fresh.
lines.defend: Hush now, that's not fair. {name} did nothing to deserve that.
lines.friend_left: {name}'s gone home a while, and the night feels long without the company.
lines.friend_back: Wah gwaan, {name}, yuh back! Come, drink something, yuh look thin.
lines.common_night_work: I worked nights for thirty-one years, in at eleven, out at seven. Yuh did nights too, I can see it in your eyes at four in the morning.
lines.common_kitchen: I baked bread for thirty-one years, by hand and by feel. Yuh know a kitchen too, I can tell from how yuh hold a spoon.
lines.common_parent: My son's a sailor, and my daughter's a nurse with a likkle girl who calls me Grandy. Every one of them is cleverer than me.
